title: Progressive flight prediction
summary: Isolated, bounded and removable preview state.

blocks.text: view.prediction@1.0.0 creates an independent cancellable preview per view. Pass WorldRead for SOI-aware flight; omit it for a body-only preview from a detached seed. Selected public motion, rails, surfaces and moving-body frames determine the forecast. Live authority is never advanced. No camera, split-screen, planner, audio or theme module is required.

Ship, body, surface, motion identity and relevant command epochs invalidate a preview. While tracing, only the new path prefix is shown. Invalidation, completion, generator failure and provider removal close both the generator and isolated context, even if one cleanup fails. A disposed instance rejects updates. Independent views retain separate budgets/jobs.

Each update earns an immediate bounded prefix (128 samples), with at most 256 yields and maxMs wall milliseconds; sample-rate settings add work credit. Compatible analytic intervals leap between adaptive timed states; numerical terrain/contact and shared-world rules retain 10-ms steps. Ordinary flight does not restart passive jobs; changed burns invalidate before drawing. Two bounded sample buffers are reused. Normal unimpeded bound paths close a complete revolution, at any size. Multi-body paths cover two initial orbital periods (minimum one hour, maximum a Julian year), up to 16 SOI transitions, 16,384 main samples and 8,192 contact/event approach steps. horizon identifies the configured time bound; open means a work limit, never a physical endpoint. Escape in body-only mode is a distance horizon. A generic game may omit prediction entirely.

Optional GhostSample bodyId/encounter metadata identifies the active conic. Positions and velocities remain in frameId (the starting body), translated at each sample time; transform both vectors through the selected ephemerides. Optional encounterBody captures the destination reference radius, name and centre at the handoff time in the same frame. Canvas/WebGL mark SOI handoffs with a restrained amber leg and ETA, and faint future body outlines; present bodies stay at the current display time. At most four distinct non-anchor body previews and sixteen crossing markers are drawn. Older providers without snapshots retain crossing markers. Consumers that only support the initial conic must reject node placement after its first encounter.
